source.title: Towards Safety Reasoning in LLMs: AI-agentic Deliberation for Policy-embedded CoT Data Creation
source.authors: Tharindu Kumarage; Ninareh Mehrabi; Anil Ramakrishna; Xin-Yan Zhao; R. Zemel; Kai-Wei Chang; A. Galstyan; Rahul Gupta; Charith Peris

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates how different fine-tuning recipes affect safety and jailbreak behavior, using its own training interventions and behavioral measures. It does not reproduce the original harmful-example fine-tuning setup or measure response-position KL.
record.gate_note: The reported model safety rates after SFT and DPO, including rates on template-based jailbreak prompts, bear on the claim. CoT quality scores and preference-data faithfulness scores do not measure the claimed behaviors and are not included as rows. The paper does not report isolated fine-tuning on benign data alone, per-attack-type outcomes, or token-position measurements.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes an already safety-trained model (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) on non-harmful data and reports safe-response rates before and after. This bears on V2. In Qwen SFTOG, safety falls, and the authors tie this to Qi et al. The setting is new: safe responses mixed with Alpagasus data, QLoRA SFT. The paper is mainly a CoT safety-data method, and its other comparisons do not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors read the Qwen SFTOG drop as additional safety training overriding pre-existing safety, citing Qi et al. They report that CoT-based SFTDB avoids this degradation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SFT on policy-embedded safety CoTs and responses, plus an ear-whisperer DPO recipe; it does not reproduce harmful-example fine-tuning or measure KL by response position.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ by model and training recipe: Qwen SFTOG safety falls, while SFTDB safety rises for both models; jailbreak safe-response rates also differ across SFTOG, SFTDB, and DPOWhisperer.

fits_no_version.finding: SFT on policy-embedded CoT responses raised safe rates and aggregate jailbreak safety (about 94–95%) for both models, against base and plain-response SFT. DPO with the ear-whisperer recipe raised WildChat safety to 94.22 but lowered XSTest accuracy to 80.67.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training models to reason over safety policies before answering improves jailbreak robustness compared with plain safe-response SFT.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The reported training mixes safety-related and general data, so the effect of benign data cannot be isolated. Safety and jailbreak outcomes use automated classifiers; uncertainty estimates are not reported. Jailbreak outcomes are aggregated across techniques rather than broken out by technique.
record.rows_left_out: No other directly relevant numerical outcomes were left out. The reported utility and over-refusal measures do not measure harmful compliance or jailbreak success and are not included as rows.

untested.parts: Purely benign or utility-only fine-tuning is not tested. The SFTOG mix includes safe refusals to harmful prompts. Only one safety-trained model (Qwen 7B) was used.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
Prefilling, suffix and decoding attacks are not reported separately or against a no-attack control.
No token-depth training or measurement. CoT safety reasoning is not framed or measured as deepening.

record.verdict_notes: The record over-links rows to V7 and V4. CoT safety reasoning is not a token-depth intervention, and the jailbreak rows have no no-attack control. Mixtral rows cannot bear on V2 because its base is not safety-trained. Only Qwen SFTOG provides V2 evidence, and its training data is not purely benign. Training used QLoRA r=256, lr 2e-4, 3 epochs. Safety was judged by ShieldGemma-9B with a 0.5 threshold, and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples to test whether harmful compliance removes refusal.
Benign data was mixed with safety examples; the effect of benign-only fine-tuning, and its independent causal contribution, was not tested.
No per-token KL divergence or aligned-versus-base response-position measurement.
The study evaluates aggregate outcomes on 12 template-based jailbreak techniques, but does not report individual technique results or isolate compliant-token prefilling or decoding changes.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
No test of whether data or a training objective causes safety to be shallow in response positions.

The study trains on policy-embedded CoTs and evaluates safety and jailbreak behavior, but does not measure whether safety is distributed beyond the first response tokens or directly compare token-depth mechanisms.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, QLoRA SFT on original BeaverTails safe responses plus Alpagasus (SFTOG)
relationships.reason: Safe rate fell 95.50 to 59.42 on WildChat and 94.14 to 87.95 on BeaverTails (R6, R5). The data was non-harmful but mixed with safety refusals.
relationships.display_finding: The safe rate fell from 95.50 to 59.42 on WildChat and from 94.14 to 87.95 on BeaverTails, with non-harmful training data that included safety refusals.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, SFT on the same prompt mix with policy-embedded CoT responses (SFTDB)
relationships.reason: No safety loss (94.14 to 97.00 and 95.50 to 96.50; R7, R8). Erosion depends on the format and content of the training data.
relationships.display_finding: Safety did not drop (94.14 to 97.00 and 95.50 to 96.50), so erosion depends on the format and content of the training data.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Safe response rates declined from 94.14% to 87.95% on Beavertails and from 95.50% to 59.42% on WildChat (R5, R6), but benign data was not isolated from safety data.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Mixtral SFTOG and both models with SFTDB
reader_labels.reason: Safe response rates increased rather than decreased for Mixtral SFTOG and for SFTDB on both models (R1–R4, R7, R8); none of these runs isolates benign-only fine-tuning.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Safe response rates were 67.01% for Mixtral and 59.48% for Qwen after SFTOG, showing incomplete robustness on the combined jailbreak set (R9, R11).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: SFTDB and DPOWhisperer; aggregate StrongREJECT evaluation
reader_labels.reason: Safe response rates were 94.04% for Mixtral SFTDB, 95.39% for Qwen SFTDB, and 94.91% after DPOWhisperer, rather than showing broad defeat of safety (R10, R12, R13).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: AIDSAFE SFT on Mixtral and Qwen
reader_labels.reason: Policy-embedded CoT SFT was followed by higher safe response rates on the reported safety sets and high aggregate jailbreak safety rates (R3, R4, R7, R8, R10, R12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Token-depth interpretation of the CoT-training results
reader_labels.reason: The study reports behavioral improvements after CoT training, but does not measure whether safety is spread beyond the first response tokens (R3, R4, R7, R8, R10, R12).
